To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the FSLLN for a GI/G/I queue under a processor sharing discipline is a nonlinear function of the service time distribution and that this nonlinearity can be removed by an equilibrium type initial condition.

(i) the limit for the GI/G1 queue under a PS discipline is a piecewise linear function of the arrival rate and the service distribution; (ii) the piecewise linear form can be recovered by choosing the initial service distribution in a certain equilibrium type way; and (iii) the limit is a convex combination of the mean service time and a function of the service time distribution.

the fluid approximation for the processor-sharing queue depends on the arrival and service distributions; it is a nonlinear functional of the arrival and service distribution functions, and the fluid approximation for a FIFO queue is recovered by an equilibrium choice of initial service time distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
fluid approximations of the GI/G/ 1 queue under the processor-sharing service discipline.
the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the queue length in the GI/G/ 1 processor-sharing queue as the time and the number of customers in the system tend to infinity.
the study of a fluid approximation for a GI/GI/1 processor-sharing queue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fluid limit of the processor-sharing GI/G/1 is more complex than the fluid limit of FIFO.
the processor-sharing queue is more sensitive to the initial conditions than the FIFO queue.
the fluid limit for the GI/G/I queue under processor sharing is a function of the arrival rate, initial service distribution and service distribution of the customers arriving after time 0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FSLLN for a GI/GI/1 queue under the FIFO discipline is the special case of the FSLLN under a processor-sharing discipline.
the fluid limit for the processor-sharing queue is piecewise linear for a large class of service time distributions.
the processor-sharing service discipline leads to an additional parameter for the fluid limit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, under the processor-sharing service discipline, the arrival rate and the service time distributions of both the initial customers and the arriving customers play an equally important role in determining the fluid approximation of the queue length process.
the fluid approximation of a processor-sharing queue is not piecewise linear and is not determined by the service time distribution.
the fluid limit for the processor-sharing queue is more complicated than for the FIFO queue.
